cases.title: Bluetooth: missed cpu_to_le16 conversion in hci_init4_req

source_evidence.observation: hdev->le_max_tx_len/time assigned directly into cp.tx_len/time; hci_req_add sends sizeof(cp), &cp
LE Write Default Data Length opcode 0x2024; packed cp.tx_len and cp.tx_time are __le16
hci_req_add forwards payload, and hci_prepare_cmd uses skb_put_data(skb,param,plen)
skb_put_data performs memcpy without byte-order conversion

cases.normal_counterexample: On little-endian, original and repaired bytes agree; with parent defaults 0x001b and 0x0148, big-endian direct-copy bytes would be 00 1b and 01 48, versus required little-endian 1b 00 and 48 01.
cases.repair: The fix wraps both assignments in cpu_to_le16.

cases.title: Bluetooth: Devcoredump: Fix storing u32 without specifying byte order issue

source_evidence.observation: hci_devcd_init writes host u32 dump_size via skb_put_data, marks INIT, and enqueues on hdev->dump.dump_q
same-host workqueue dequeues and dispatches INIT to hci_devcd_handle_pkt_init
consumer casts pulled bytes to u32*, reads numeric value, then calls hci_devcd_prepare

cases.normal_counterexample: The old host-byte producer and host-u32 consumer run in one host kernel, so a big-endian producer/consumer pair reads back the same numeric dump_size, subject to alignment behavior not proved here.
cases.repair: Fix changes the pair to put_unaligned_le32/get_unaligned_le32, specifying little-endian bytes and unaligned-safe access.
